title: The Broken Trail
premise: Noor Galloway, a bush pilot who has spent a decade outrunning grief in the interior of a fractured country, salvages a chest from the river bearing the seal of Vaskaria — a nation erased by treaty and buried under the mountains. Inside are documents proving the drowned kingdom's heirs still live, and a map to its forbidden source, guarded by the very government that destroyed it. Pursued by a corrupt minister's agents and accompanied by Sefa, a river guide whose family died keeping Vaskarian secrets, Noor must choose between flying home to safety and following the water upstream. At the source they find not treasure but survivors: a hidden community that offers Noor the belonging they never knew they wanted — at the cost of becoming a target forever. In the end, Noor chooses to stay grounded for the first time in ten years, while Sefa carries the truth downstream to spark a reckoning.
about_author: Freya Halloran is a former floatplane dispatcher who spent six years in remote northern communities before turning to fiction full-time. Her work explores rivers as both roads and witnesses, and she writes from a cabin reachable only by boat.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: POV Noor. A routine medicine run over the interior establishes Noor's solitary life, their rule against attachments, and their encyclopedic knowledge of the river country. A storm forces an unplanned landing near a drowned village no longer on maps. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for freedom; the first crack in Noor's armor appears when they linger too long at the shoreline.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Fishing nets snag a sealed chest stamped with the Vaskarian crest. Before Noor can decide what to do with it, Sefa arrives asking pointed questions about salvage rights — and about who else has seen it. Emotional beat: wary attraction and mutual suspicion; two people each holding half a secret, circling each other like weather fronts.

chapters.title: The Minister's Men
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Government agents arrive in town led by the charming, ruthless Deputy Minister Corven Hale, who offers Noor a fortune for the chest and lets slip how much blood was spilled to bury Vaskaria. That night someone searches Noor's hangar. Emotional beat: dread replacing curiosity; Noor realizes the chest isn't history, it's a live grenade.

chapters.title: Paper Kingdoms
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Opening the chest with Sefa reveals census records, photographs, and a letter naming living heirs hidden 'where the water is born.' The documents also implicate Hale's ministry in the erasure itself. Emotional beat: awe curdling into anger; Noor, who trusts nothing but instruments and distance, begins to believe in something worth risking for.

chapters.title: Fuel, Lies, and Departure
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Preparing to fly upstream means lying to fuel clerks, bribing a weather station, and leaving Noor's beloved plane behind at the last navigable strip — the river beyond is canyon-locked. Hale's men burn a informant's boat as a message. Emotional beat: commitment; the point of no return crossed quietly, with packed bags and unspoken fear.

chapters.title: The Canyon Refuses Strangers
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Rapids, portages, and a rockslide nearly kill them; Sefa saves Noor and confesses their family were Vaskarian keepers who died for less than what Noor now carries. They argue bitterly about whether truth or survival matters more. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in danger; love admitted sideways, in the middle of a fight neither wants to win.

chapters.title: Where the Water Is Born
chapters.summary: POV Noor. They reach the source: a hidden valley where Vaskarian descendants have lived undetected for a generation, led by an aging heir, Mirela, who greets the documents like returning children. But Mirela refuses to let the evidence leave — exposure would mean extermination. Emotional beat: wonder and heartbreak; Noor finds the belonging they always fled from, and learns it demands sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Hale's expedition closes in using satellite tracking and a traitor inside the valley. Mirela proposes a terrible bargain: destroy the documents and stay silent forever, or send them out and doom everyone. Noor volunteers to be the decoy carrying fakes downstream. Emotional beat: duty versus love made literal; Sefa must decide whether to let Noor go.

chapters.title: Corven Hale's River
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The decoy run becomes a chase through fog and rapids; captured, Noor stalls Hale with the forged papers long enough for Sefa and valley scouts to disable his boats upstream. Confronted with proof his own career was built on massacre, Hale chooses escalation over retreat. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into defiance; Noor stops measuring escape routes and stands their ground.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: POV Noor and Sefa, alternating. Hale's downfall comes not from violence but from the documents reaching a journalist via the river network he underestimated; the valley survives, its existence now protected by public outrage rather than secrecy. Noor sells the plane, keeps one crate of medicine runs, and unpacks — truly unpacks — for the first time in ten years. Emotional beat: resolution; love against duty resolved not by choosing one, but by discovering they were the same choice all along.
